what: An svg line drawing placed in the panel is baked into one Lottie and looped endlessly at 5 seconds (30fps, 150 frames). Lines are drawn and then erased behind (sweep), shapes swell and shrink like breathing (pulse), spin, sway, drift, blink, and circles spread and fade (ripple). Clicking the panel (Enter and Space too) pauses it in place, and clicking again resumes (react-lottie click-to-pause). The black-filled head is layered in svg order so it hides the lines behind it. Color and weight read the svg’s computed stroke and fill, so they follow the skin.

options.ease: Per-layer key curve x1,y1,x2,y2, default .333,0,.667,1 (After Effects default smooth key)
options.click: If none, pressing does not stop it
options.[data-fx-part=art]: Svg to bake — viewBox required. The shapes inside (path · line · polyline · polygon · circle · ellipse · rect, with rounded corners made as path) and <g transform> Read
options.[data-kind]: one layer (all shapes inside a g face) — sweep|draw|pulse|spin|sway|drift|blink|ripple. data-at (start sec) · data-dur (length sec) · data-to (pulse·ripple scale %, spin angle, sway angle, blink opacity %) · data-from (drift offset "dx,dy")·data-origin (axis "x,y", default layer center)·data-ease
options.[data-sweep]: Line wipe on just one shape inside the layer — data-at, data-dur (length of the drawing, erasing takes the same length)

note: The original is eight Lottie JSON files exported from After Effects (gray 3px line drawings of a side-face profile with the head at center) — the artwork can’t be carried over, so the svg for the consuming side is baked. With reduced motion the svg is left as is (a still image). The svg shows even without Lottie. The original gradient line (ends fade out) is baked as a solid line.
